newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power plummets on holiday, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power plummets on holiday, weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. continued to soften sharply Monday, due to revised weather forecasts, the upcoming holiday, softer gas prices and a return of some nuclear power, sources said.
"There's just no demand. A lot of people are trying to schedule their stuff through Friday," one source said, noting some utilities would be closed Tuesday through Thursday.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Tuesday were sharply lower in the $9.50-10.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Friday's $16.00-17.00 trading range.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed at $8.00 or lower, but no deals could be confirmed done.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Tuesday delivery plummeted into the $16.00-18.00 range, as compared with the $24.00-25.00 trading range on Friday.
Firm, off-peak power for Tuesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed at $9.00, but most traders were concentrating on peak business.
Despite last week's threat of a cold front this week, forecasters are now calling for only a slight drop in temperatures on Wednesday, dipping about five degrees below normal.
More moderate temperatures are forecast from Thursday through the early part of next week.
Like power prices, natural gas spot values in south Texas fell by about 40 cents today to the low-$3.80s per million British thermal units.
Separately, Carolina Power and Light's 880 megawatt (MW) Harris 1 nuclear power unit in New Hill, N.C., was expected to reach full power today.
Also, Virginia Power's Surry 2 (781 MW) and North Anna 2 (909 MW) have both restarted, with North Anna expected to reach full power Tuesday.
Also returning to the grid and operating near full power is the 1,129 MW Catawba 2 nuclear unit in Clover, S.C.
